sec: Hormone replacement protocols, corticosteroid equivalents and Nelson syndrome

items.q: What is the standard daily oral hydrocortisone replacement regimen in panhypopituitarism designed to replicate endogenous circadian rhythm?
opts: 10 mg morning, 5 mg afternoon, 5 mg evening (10-5-5 regimen)
5 mg four times daily every 6 hours
items.exp: The 10-5-5 hydrocortisone regimen (10 mg morning, 5 mg afternoon, 5 mg evening) replicates normal endogenous cortisol rhythm. (Book p957)

items.q: If a patient on maintenance hydrocortisone replacement develops an acute systemic infection, how should their steroid dose be adjusted?
opts: Double the dose (and triple for very severe infections)
Halve the dose to prevent immunosuppression
Withhold oral steroids until fever resolves
items.exp: In infection, double the hydrocortisone dose; triple the dose for very severe infections. (Book p957)

items.q: A patient with panhypopituitarism on oral replacement therapy develops acute gastroenteritis with intractable vomiting and hypotension. What is the immediate drug administration route required?
opts: Increase oral hydrocortisone to four times daily
Administer oral fludrocortisone with rehydration salts
items.exp: If vomiting or hypotension occurs, hydrocortisone must be administered intravenously. (Book p957)

items.q: What is the standard daily replacement dose of levothyroxine in secondary hypothyroidism?
items.exp: Levothyroxine replacement dose is 50-200 ug/day. (Book p957)

items.q: Match the glucocorticoid to its equivalent anti-inflammatory dose — 1) Dexamethasone 2) Methylprednisolone 3) Prednisolone 4) Hydrocortisone … A) 0.75 mg B) 4 mg C) 5 mg D) 20 mg
items.exp: Equivalent doses are Dexamethasone 0.75 mg = Methylprednisolone 4 mg = Prednisolone 5 mg = Hydrocortisone 20 mg = Cortisone 25 mg. (Book p957)

items.q: What equivalent dose of cortisone corresponds to 20 mg of hydrocortisone?
items.exp: Cortisone 25 mg is biologically equivalent to 20 mg of hydrocortisone. (Book p957)

items.q: For central diabetes insipidus in hypopituitarism, what is the standard desmopressin dosing?
opts: Nasal desmopressin 20 ug or 0.1 to 0.2 mg PO
items.exp: ADH replacement is given as nasal desmopressin 20 ug or 0.1-0.2 mg PO. (Book p957)

items.q: What is the pediatric growth hormone replacement dosing range aimed at achieving > 12 cm height velocity per year?
items.exp: Children receive 0.18-0.35 mg/kg/week SC targeting > 12 cm height increase/year (adults receive 0.3 mg/day SC). (Book p957)

items.q: Which adverse effect is NOT typically associated with growth hormone replacement therapy in children?
items.exp: GH replacement side effects include BIH, hypertension, and scoliosis; agranulocytosis is not a side effect. (Book p957)

items.q: A 42-year-old female who underwent bilateral adrenalectomy for refractory Cushing disease two years ago presents with profound generalized hyperpigmentation of her abdominal surgical scar and bitemporal hemianopsia. Sellar MRI reveals an aggressive macroadenoma. What condition is this?
items.exp: Nelson syndrome occurs post bilateral adrenalectomy due to loss of negative feedback, resulting in massive ACTH elevation, pituitary tumor expansion, and intense hyperpigmentation. (Book p957)

items.q: Nelson syndrome arises from loss of negative feedback following bilateral adrenalectomy, causing hypersecretion of ___ and corticotroph tumor growth.
items.exp: Loss of adrenal negative feedback leads to uncontrolled ACTH hypersecretion in Nelson syndrome. (Book p957)

items.q: Assess hormone replacement priorities in hypopituitarism: I Corticosteroid replacement must ALWAYS be initiated prior to starting levothyroxine to prevent precipitating adrenal crisis. II If fertility is desired in gonadotroph deficiency, therapy utilizes hCG or GnRH.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Steroids must precede thyroxine to prevent adrenal crisis; when fertility is desired, hCG or GnRH is administered. (Book p957)
